fact: Organic Law 2004-63 of 27 July 2004, arts. 50-52, bars transfer of personal data abroad where it harms public security or Tunisia's vital interests, allows it only to a country with an adequate level of protection, and requires prior authorisation of the data protection authority (INPDP) in every case, decided within one month; the document notes no replacement law had been adopted at its 2026 retrieval.
The DIAL article (published 2026-06-15) says Tunisia's 2018 adequacy list of countries for data transfers identified only five African countries.
Lawyer Zied El Air says the 2004 data protection law has an outdated regime for international transfers.
Lawyer Zied El Air says organic bill No. 095/2025, before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee, contains a revised framework for international transfers.

Article 21 of decree-law 2022-2 of 4 January 2022 bars credit information companies from transferring their databases, or setting up sites to protect the data given to them, outside Tunisia, and bars them from hosting credit information in the cloud.

The African Union Commission's status list of 02/02/2026 records Tunisia as having signed the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention) on 23/04/2019, with no date of ratification or accession and no date of deposit; 20 of 55 states have ratified or acceded.
